 Judgment
Dated this the 06th day of February, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.48/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Pala is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal)
2.
The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 29.08.2011.

According to the petitioner, on 29.08.2011, at about 07.45 p.m., while he was walking through the side of Kudamaloor - Panambalam public road, a car bearing No.KL-5/Y-3400 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner, hit him down.
As a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3. The 2nd respondent is the owner and the 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of 2025:KER:12762 compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.4,03,000/- and is limited to 3,000,00/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1, and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A16.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.
6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.95,450/-.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
9. Heard Sri.Thomas Abraham, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.P.Jacob Mathew, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was working as Coolie, earning Rs.9,000/- per month, but the Tribunal fixed his monthly income at Rs.5,000/-.

Since he could not prove his job or income as claimed in the OP, in the light of a dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], his notional income is liable to be fixed as that of a coolie, at Rs.8,000/-.
12.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
Tenderness right supracondylar area right femur, abnormal mobility +, multiple abrasions over left foot, X-ray showed supra-condylar fracture right femur.
Old mal-united fracture both bones of right leg.

Ext.A7 is the discharge card which shows that the petitioner had sustained comminuted supra-condylar fractue right femur and old mal-united cross 2025:KER:12762 united fracture both bones of right leg.
The Tribunal assessed his disability at 5% and it is not under challenge.
13. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 49 years.

Therefore, 25 % of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 13, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, (2009) 6 SCC 121.

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.78000/-.

Therefore, Rs.39,000/- awarded by the Tribunal on the head "loss of earning capacity" will be deducted from the compensation awarded on the head "loss of disability".
14.

Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/-, towards extra nourishment Rs. 1,000/- was awarded and no amount was awarded by the tribunal towards the loss of amenities.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
15. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 26 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability 2025:KER:12762 suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads loss of earnings, 'pain and sufferings', loss of amenities and extra nourishment are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.96000/-(8000x12),
50,000/-, 25,000/- and 5,000/- respectively.
16.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

17. Therefore, the petitioners/ appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.2,72,450/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.
